article_meta.title: EP 97: AI Psychosis 시대의 사람들 | AI Frontier

article_core_claims: AI coding agents and harnesses have moved from engineer-only coding tools into general knowledge-work workflow infrastructure.
Model and harness improvement cycles are compressing; frontier capability, cheaper inference, inference-chip diversity, and productized fast modes increase the amount of work that can be delegated.
The new AI application form is less a traditional app or UX surface and more a workflow/task-completion harness driven by user intent.
Vertical AI products will differentiate through exclusive customer data, proprietary tool combinations, and control layers that general agents such as Codex or Claude cannot fully access.

AI-native workflows differ from AI-assisted workflows: AI-native means the workflow completes with minimal human intervention, while many enterprise efforts merely patch AI onto unchanged human processes.
The relevant talent bar is rising from basic Claude Code/Codex usage to domain judgment, infrastructure awareness, meta-optimization, and the ability to decide under uncertainty.
High-speed delegation creates human bottlenecks: T_brain, bio-token depletion, context switching, burnout, FOMO, shallow learning, and AI-psychosis-like overdelegation.

Mitchell Hashimoto and Mario Zechner-style concerns pressure the assumption that test-passing AI output is enough; architecture, maintainability, and hidden debt can degrade while surface behavior passes.
Slow AI and mind-sized bites are emerging as a counterpressure: work and learning should be sized to what the human operator can actually absorb.
As building becomes commoditized, brand, distribution, positioning, and subculture/world creation become more important.
recommended_changes_to_space_reading: Add a T_brain/operator-load note to future space-impact readings: expected review burden, context switches, and whether the next action is absorbable by the operator.
Extend heavy-trigger language to include maintainability/architecture pressure even when local tests or agent consensus pass.
When post-review is skipped by budget gate, include an explicit residual-risk line for hidden architecture debt and human comprehension debt.
Add a slow-AI/mind-sized-bite recommendation field or rubric for recovery cards: the next safe lane should be not only safe from authority mutation, but also small enough to review.
Treat AI-native versus AI-assisted as a recurring classification in VectorFL readings: is the process actually completing a workflow, or merely producing assistive artifacts?
Preserve the current no-call/read-only lane for article impact reads unless the article introduces concrete architectural ambiguity or promotion pressure.
risks: Over-indexing on actual multi-agent participation could recreate the article's overdelegation problem and increase operator fatigue.
Agent agreement may be mistaken for correctness if maintainability and architecture coherence are not separately reviewed.
Budget gates based mostly on elapsed seconds can miss human cognitive cost.
Vertical/control-layer language could pressure premature promotion of VectorFL artifacts into authority; this should remain blocked under HOLD.
The article is conversational and partly speculative, so it should pressure heuristics and reading posture rather than directly update authoritative space state.

space_impact.authority_effect: No authority, registry, endpoint, current-position, or promotion change is warranted from this article alone.
space_impact.hold_status: Remain HOLD; use as evidence/reading pressure only.
space_impact.net_effect: VectorFL should keep FAST_NO_CALL_LOCAL_VALIDATION as default and heavy actual multi-agent mode as gated, but space readings should now explicitly score T_brain, mind-sizedness, and hidden maintainability risk alongside drift, trace, and authority boundaries.
space_impact.summary: The article does not overturn VectorFL's current direction; it strengthens it while adding a human-load and maintainability pressure layer.

vectorfl_alignment_points: The article strongly aligns with VectorFL's move from content-only processing to actual process/harness behavior: VectorFL evidence already distinguishes VectorFL-as-content from actual Hermes/Codex/Gemini participation.
The article's harness-as-control-layer thesis aligns with VectorFL's four-shape loop, safe entrypoints, receipts, trace rows, and HOLD boundaries as a control surface rather than a passive report.

The article's T_brain and bio-token bottleneck maps directly onto VectorFL's budget gate: fast local validation should remain default, while heavy multi-agent calls should be reserved for ambiguity, architecture pressure, drift, or explicit user request.

The article's maintainability warning reinforces VectorFL's repeatability and drift posture: pass/fail outputs are insufficient unless traceability, receipt integrity, and layer rereading remain visible.
The article's distinction between AI-native and AI-assisted workflows supports VectorFL's pressure to make Hermes processing itself VectorFL-like, not merely to produce artifacts about VectorFL.
The article's slow-AI/mind-sized-bites frame supports operator-facing recovery cards and compact handoff packets as first-class artifacts.
vectorfl_pressure_points: Current VectorFL evidence is strong on process validation, but the article pressures it to account explicitly for human operator load, not only external agent seconds and validation checks.
The budget gate measures Codex/Gemini/Hermes time well, but it does not yet expose T_brain cost: review burden, context-switch count, decision fatigue, and whether a result is mind-sized.

The heavy-trigger list includes architecture and drift pressure, but the article suggests another trigger class: maintainability/hidden-debt pressure when outputs pass locally but architecture may be degrading.
The operator surface is display-only and safe, but the article implies recovery surfaces should also help the operator choose slower, smaller, more absorbable next actions.
VectorFL's current framing of AI readiness as actual agent participation may underweight the article's warning that stronger delegation can create shallow understanding and false completion.
Post-review is currently skipped when agents agree and no drift appears; the article pressures this rule because agent agreement can still miss architectural incoherence or overdelegation risk.

gemini_layer_impact.ai_psychosis_guard_implication: The psychosis guard is implemented via the 'Validator Gate' and the refusal to allow agents to self-promote artifacts to 'Authority'. By treating agent output as 'Raw Trace' until human-inspected, VectorFL prevents the 'slot machine' dopamine loop of unverified task completion.
gemini_layer_impact.layer_reading: The article's projection of 'AI Surface' replacing traditional apps aligns with VectorFL's 'Operator Surface' (Evidence 3), where interaction is via hardened artifacts rather than UI widgets. The shift toward 'Meta-Optimizers' validates the Hermes-centered interpretation loop, where the agent discovers paths (Logic Layer) while the space provides the 'unbundled Oracle' (Data/Reference Layer).
gemini_layer_impact.slow_ai_implication: VectorFL's 'mind-sized bites' approach—breaking work into Intent, Packet, and Receipt—is the architectural implementation of 'Slow AI'. It forces a 'T_brain' break-even point where the operator can digest and validate the model's 'elite sprint' before it manifests in the space.
gemini_layer_impact.spatial_effect_on_vectorfl: VectorFL transitions from a content-management system to a 'Slow AI' regulator. The 'Budget Gate' (Evidence 2) specifically addresses the T_brain bottleneck by determining when to use expensive multi-agent heavy reading versus fast local validation. The 'HOLD' boundary becomes the primary defense against the 'AI Psychosis' of blind model-driven mutation.
gemini_layer_impact.tension_map: Acceleration vs. Rot: 2-month release cycles (GPT-5.6) create a 'T_brain' bottleneck, where human judgment cannot scale with model speed. Delegation vs. Mastery: 'AI Psychosis' (Karpathy's total delegation) tensions against Mitchell Hashimoto's warning that AI-generated architectures can look correct while being fundamentally broken.
gemini_layer_impact.what_becomes_more_important: Hardened receipts and repeatability reports (3/3 pass in Evidence 3) become the only way to verify 'jagged' model performance. Vertical tool-combination (Unbundling) becomes the primary differentiator for space-resident skills over general model capabilities.
gemini_layer_impact.what_should_not_change: The hierarchy of authority (Constitution > Baseline) must remain absolute. Evidence reinsertion must stay in the 'HOLD' lane (Evidence 1) to prevent the acceleration loops described in the article from eroding the space's structural integrity.

hermes_merged_space_impact.recommended_next: create a compact candidate lens card for T_brain + mind-sizedness + maintainability debt, still HOLD.
hermes_merged_space_impact.space_effect: Strengthens VectorFL as harness/control layer and adds human-load/maintainability pressure to budget gate and operator surfaces.
